solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Legislators make progress slowly at first

blocks.clueFragment: Legislators make progress slowly at first
blocks.note: surface reading: lawmakers are slow to get going
setter's reading: the chamber where a bill has its first, slow readings before moving on

explanation.surface: A grumble that politicians are sluggish whenever they start something new.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain most bills start in the elected lower chamber and inch through first and second readings there before going elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The elected lower chamber of the UK Parliament is made up of its members, the people who pass laws.

clue.text: One from country, alpine, high

indicators.note: high can mean drunk or intoxicated, so the word before it is reeling into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone from a mountainous country lives high up in alpine terrain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' sits naturally beside 'alpine' as altitude, but here it means intoxicated.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Himalayan kingdom between India and Tibet is described by this nationality word.

clue.text: Travelling. seek a man, one with something nominally in common

definitions.text: one with something nominally in common

indicators.note: letters that are travelling are on the move, so they shift into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller goes looking for a man who happens to share something with them.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who bears the same given name or surname as another shares only a label, a punning sense of nominal.

clue.text: Olive, shy, music transformed in playful way

indicators.note: transformed means changed in form, so the three words before it are rebuilt into another order

blocks.note: taken as written, all three words

explanation.surface: A timid woman named Olive is changed by music into someone playful.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with impish, teasing naughtiness is behaving in a playful manner, an adverb matching the clue phrase.

clue.text: Notes golden shooting star

blocks.note: two sol-fa notes, me (mi) and te
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Golden musical notes are likened to a shooting star.
explanation.definitionFit: A streak of light from space debris burning up in the atmosphere is popularly called a shooting star.

clue.text: They’re well-read, to some extent elite, rationalistic

indicators.note: to some extent says only part of the following words is used, a run of letters within them

blocks.note: the run straddles the two words, ignoring the comma

explanation.surface: Bookish people are said to be somewhat elitist and rationalist.
explanation.definitionFit: The learned, bookish intellectual class is a plural noun for people who read widely.

clue.text: Off topic about period referring to Tosca?

indicators.note: off means gone bad or wrong, so the word after it is rearranged
about means going around, so the rearranged word wraps around the next piece

blocks.note: the five letters of topic, rearranged
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone straying from the subject of a historical period while discussing a famous work.
explanation.walkthrough: Tosca is Puccini's opera, so the question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosca is a Puccini opera, so anything relating to it is of the opera, as the adjective says.

clue.text: Sign minutes in India after meeting, tiresome ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the closing letters of the two words before it are kept

blocks.note: last letter of meeting
last letter of tiresome
standard abbreviation for minutes
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Minutes are signed off in India after a tedious meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the minutes and India after the two final letters; 'ultimately' applies to both meeting and tiresome.
explanation.definitionFit: The Twins is one of the twelve zodiac signs, the astrological period around late May and June.

clue.text: Dreadful crime, person’s to investigate it — him?

definitions.text: Dreadful crime, person’s to investigate it — him?

indicators.note: dreadful means terrible or awful, so the letters following it are mangled into another order

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the punctuation

explanation.surface: A grim murder has happened, and someone must look into it; who might that detective be?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also reads as the description: a terrible crime needs a person to investigate it, and he is the one.
explanation.definitionFit: Colin Dexter's Oxford detective, famous from novels and TV, is the classic figure who investigates terrible murders.

clue.text: Hurry! Mollify media boss, easily angered

blocks.note: 'Quick!' is a command to hurry
to temper is to soften or moderate
ed is short for editor, the boss of a newspaper

explanation.surface: An urgent plea to calm down a short-fused newspaper chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who flies off the handle at slight provocation has a hasty, short fuse.

clue.text: Woman carrying poster in colour

indicators.note: carrying means holding, so the first word's letters hold the next word's letters inside

blocks.note: she is the pronoun for a woman
an advertisement, such as a poster

explanation.surface: A woman holds a colourful poster.
explanation.definitionFit: A tint or hue, as in a particular variety of a hue, is another word for a colour.

clue.text: Broadcast censured about introduction of smut, being earthy

indicators.note: an introduction is the opening, so only the first letter of the next word is used
broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of the next word are strewn into a new order
about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the single letter

blocks.note: taken as written
first letter of smut

explanation.surface: A broadcast was condemned for including smutty, earthy material.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthy humour is coarse and vulgar, and the noun for that quality is the state of being coarse.

clue.text: Nice friend, at first recalling system of transferring money, folding?

indicators.note: recalling suggests calling back, so the phrase after it is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: giro is a British system of bank or post-office transfers
ami is French for friend, and Nice is a French city

explanation.surface: A friend in Nice reminisces about a money-transfer system, and asks about folding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like an adjective but is the French city, so the friend is French; 'at first' puts the reversed piece before it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese craft of shaping paper into models is all about folding, hinted at by the question mark.

clue.text: Way of charging Irish city wise? Not at first

indicators.note: not at first says to drop the opening letter of the word just before

blocks.note: Cork is a city in the south of Ireland
sage means wise

explanation.surface: Asking how an Irish city sets its charges, and whether that is wise.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant fee levied for opening wine a diner brings in themselves is a particular charge or fee.

clue.text: Campaigner’s unusual action isn’t over — Greens finally to be involved

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the closing letter of the preceding word counts
unusual means out of the ordinary, so the following letters are set in an unfamiliar order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, dropping the apostrophe
taken as written
last letter of Greens

explanation.surface: An environmental activist says the unusual protest is not finished and the Green party must get involved.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay; 'to be involved' adds the final S to the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who campaigns to protect nature and the environment is an activist for its preservation.

clue.text: Viking, maybe, one riding, getting new start

indicators.note: getting a new start means the opening letter is swapped for another one

blocks.note: a rider on horseback
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A Viking on horseback gets a fresh beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval Scandinavian, of whom the seafaring raider is one example, hence 'maybe' for definition by example.

clue.text: Speak about knight, extremely lazy, in high-flown way

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word's letters surround the following piece
extremely refers to the extremes, so only the two end letters of the next word are kept

blocks.note: to orate is to speak formally
N is the chess notation for a knight
first and last letters of lazy

explanation.surface: Someone speaks pompously about a very lazy knight.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand, flowery language is elaborately decorated, so speaking that way is speaking with elaborate decoration.

clue.text: Letters from Myanmar about flier

indicators.note: letters from says the result is taken directly out of the words that follow

blocks.note: the run spans the end of the first word and most of the second

explanation.surface: Correspondence from Myanmar concerning an airman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters' suggests mail and 'flier' a pilot, but the flier is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A large African stork is a bird, so a creature that flies, a flier.

clue.text: Initially bit like sheep, like cattle

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: first letter of bit
ovine is the adjective for sheep

explanation.surface: Something starts out a bit sheeplike and ends up like a cow.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relating to cows and oxen also describes dull, placid behaviour typical of those animals.

clue.text: Screen pupil assisting teacher

blocks.note: first meaning: a display for a computer
second meaning: a schoolchild given a duty to help in class

explanation.surface: A pupil helps a teacher set up a classroom display.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a computer display unit and a schoolchild given small duties to help staff.

clue.text: Caustic about, for example, upcoming objective

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means read from bottom to top
about means around, so the first word's letters go round the next piece

blocks.note: tart means sharp or cutting in tone
e.g. abbreviates for example

explanation.surface: A sharp remark about an example of an upcoming aim.
explanation.definitionFit: An aim or goal one is trying to hit is a mark to shoot for, a noun matching the clue word.

clue.text: Have excessive regard for exotic oeuvre, lavish, half-finished

indicators.note: half-finished means only the front half was done, so just the first half of that word stays
exotic means strange and foreign, so the letters are made unfamiliar by reordering

blocks.note: taken as written
first half of lavish

explanation.surface: Rating too highly a lavish, exotic body of artistic work that was never completed.
explanation.definitionFit: To think something worth more than it is, is to esteem it too highly, a verb phrase matching the clue.

clue.text: Something incomplete that one regrets, setting off originally

indicators.note: originally means at the origin, so each of the preceding words gives just its opening letter

blocks.note: first letter
first letter
first letter
first letter
first letter

explanation.surface: A half-finished project that someone wishes they had never begun.
explanation.definitionFit: A sculpture of just the trunk, or any unfinished work, lacks its head and limbs, so is unfinished.

clue.text: Spots substitutes, losing heart

indicators.note: losing heart means the middle of the word is removed

blocks.note: stand-ins are substitutes

explanation.surface: A coach picks out substitutes who have lost their spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart is the middle two letters of the eight-letter word.
explanation.definitionFit: Marks or blemishes on cloth are dirty patches, the plural noun matching the clue word.

clue.text: They give answers in relation to hand tool

blocks.note: re means concerning or regarding
a gripping tool used by hand

explanation.surface: People respond to questions about a hand tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who respond to letters or questions are respondents, people who answer.
